questions.question: Who are the parties to this agreement?
questions.expected_answer: Party A Corporation and Party B Industries.

questions.question: When does the agreement take effect?
Why are the parties sharing information?
questions.expected_answer: To evaluate a potential business relationship or transaction (the Purpose).

questions.question: Where is Party B located?
What counts as confidential information?
questions.expected_answer: Proprietary information, technical data, trade secrets or know-how disclosed by one party that is marked confidential or should reasonably be understood as confidential.

questions.question: Does something told to me verbally also count as confidential?
questions.expected_answer: Yes, information disclosed orally is included.

questions.question: Who am I allowed to share confidential information with?
questions.expected_answer: Only employees, directors or advisors with a need to know who are bound by similar confidentiality obligations.

questions.question: Can I tell my friend about the project?
questions.expected_answer: No; only employees, directors or advisors with a need to know may receive it.

questions.question: Can I use the information for my own side project?
questions.expected_answer: No; it may be used only for the business Purpose.

questions.question: How carefully do I have to protect the information?
questions.expected_answer: With at least the same care as its own confidential information, and never less than reasonable care.

questions.question: What information is not considered confidential?
questions.expected_answer: Public information, information already lawfully held, information received from a third party without restriction, or independently developed information.

questions.question: If the information is already on the internet, do I still have to keep it secret?
questions.expected_answer: No; publicly known information is excluded.

questions.question: What if I came up with the same idea myself?
How long do I have to keep the information secret?
questions.expected_answer: Three years from the date of disclosure, or until released in writing.

questions.question: Can I terminate?
questions.expected_answer: There is no early termination right; confidentiality lasts 3 years or until a written release.

questions.question: Can the other side free me from the secrecy duty early?
questions.expected_answer: Yes, the Disclosing Party can release the Receiving Party in writing.
